name: Ahithophel
overview: Ahithophel was a trusted counselor to King David, known for his wise and influential advice, as seen when Absalom summoned him during his rebellion (2 Samuel 15:12,16:20). Despite his previous loyalty, Ahithophel joined Absalom's conspiracy against David, offering counsel that aimed to weaken David's position, such as advising Absalom to publicly dishonor his father by taking his concubines (2 Samuel 16:21). David, recognizing the danger of Ahithophel's counsel, earnestly prayed that the Lord would turn it into foolishness, highlighting the spiritual battle behind the political conflict (2 Samuel 15:31,34). The narrative also alludes to Ahithophel’s tragic end by suicide, underscoring the consequences of turning away from God's purposes.
